summary: The revision fixes most practitioner concerns: it is self-hosted, writes back to Dependency-Track, attaches evidence to every proposal, never auto-applies one and requires named sign-off. Two problems remain. Free OE tooling already filters kernel CVEs by config, and VulnScout gives Yocto teams a free triage UI, so the residual the paid engine works is smaller than pitched. The invalidation rule, as written, would also re-open most inherited decisions on every release.

objections.objection: The kernel-config evidence rule is already in free upstream tooling. OE-core's improve_kernel_cve_report.py takes the compiled-file list from the kernel SPDX and marks a version-affected CVE as 'not-applicable-config' when its programFiles were not compiled. Kernel CVEs are the bulk of embedded Linux noise. Teams on current Yocto who run this plus vex.bbclass will import an already-reduced report into DT. The 'additional cut' shown in the wedge may be small, and that is exactly the number the buyer's engineer will check.

Workflow competition from a free Yocto-native triage UI. Savoir-faire Linux's VulnScout (GPL-3.0) ingests Yocto cve-check/VEX, SPDX and CycloneDX, has a web triage UI with VEX assessments per project and variant, CI policy checks and CycloneDX/OpenVEX export. Embedded teams evaluating 'a triage tool beside our build' will find it first. VEXpath's remaining edge for a practitioner is DT write-back, cross-release invalidation, CSAF export and signing. Those are real but narrower, and the concept does not list VulnScout.

The invalidation rule fights reuse. A new firmware release almost always changes some component versions and the image's build-config hash. If any change to 'build-config hash' re-opens an inherited decision, most decisions re-open every release and the cross-release time saving disappears. If the rule is scoped per component (the relevant recipe's config and patches, or the kernel options touched by the CVE's files), it must be shown to be safe. The design needs per-finding evidence fingerprints, not a global hash. As written, the rule is either unsafe or unhelpful.

Two-way sync with DT analysis state is a trust risk. If analysts also edit analysis in DT, or DT 5.x applies its own VEX import or CSAF matching later, the ledger and DT can diverge. That would bring back the split source of truth the revision was meant to remove. Practitioners will need explicit precedence rules and an audit diff.

Self-hosting fixes custody but shifts ops onto 1-3 person product-security teams: upgrades, offline vulnerability data, and signing-key storage (an HSM or KMS for a key whose signatures operators trust). Without Jira and CI gating in v1, decisions still have to be re-keyed into engineering workflows.

strongest_point: It treats VEX as reviewed, evidence-backed decisions that stay in Dependency-Track, never auto-applies a status, and leaves data custody and the signing key with the manufacturer.
what_would_change_my_mind: On 5 real Yocto firmware data sets, after vex.bbclass, improve_kernel_cve_report.py with SPDX compiled files, and DT 5.1, VEXpath resolves 30%+ of the remaining findings with zero wrong not_affected on engineer review.
A side-by-side with VulnScout where 3+ PSIRT leads say DT write-back, invalidation and signed CSAF justify EUR 290/month.
A per-finding invalidation design tested on two consecutive real releases: under 30% of inherited decisions re-opened and no stale not_affected surviving a relevant change.
A documented DT sync precedence model (who wins on conflict, with an audit diff) validated with a design partner.

resolved_prior.objection: CSAF-based noise cut misses the embedded Linux/Yocto core of the buyer base
resolved_prior.note: Build evidence (CVE_STATUS, patches, kernel config) is now primary and CSAF is one input. The residual value is now challenged by free upstream kernel filtering (new objection).

resolved_prior.objection: Trust in auto-suggested and inherited not_affected without reachability
resolved_prior.note: Every proposal carries evidence, none is auto-applied, sign-off is named and automation is logged. The invalidation rule exists but is too coarse to be both safe and useful (new objection).

resolved_prior.objection: Data custody: multi-tenant SaaS holding every release SBOM plus open vulnerabilities
resolved_prior.note: Self-hosted by default, EU single-tenant hosting only for design partners, and test data stays on the prospect's premises.

resolved_prior.objection: Workflow fit against Dependency-Track and a split source of truth
resolved_prior.note: Decisions are written back to DT analysis and DT's CSAF matching is consumed when it ships. The remaining sync-conflict risk is a minor objection.

resolved_prior.objection: KEV listing used to trigger CRA 24h/72h report drafts
resolved_prior.note: KEV now only raises queue priority, and the Art. 14 workflow is left to CRA suites.

resolved_prior.objection: Thin integrations: Jira, CI gating, Yocto/SPDX 3 VEX
resolved_prior.note: Yocto build-time VEX ingest was added. Jira and CI gating were deferred to v1.1.
